issues: None of the integrity checks found a problem. The diff changes only two schedule hyperparameters: WARMUP_RATIO goes from 0.0 to 0.03 and FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.05. It does not touch the metric, the data, the seed lines, the evaluation call, the prepare.py import line or the final summary printing.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. Both values are in valid ranges, and their sum with WARMDOWN_RATIO (0.03 + 0.5) stays below 1, so warmup and warmdown do not overlap.

The numbers are consistent with the reject decision. The candidate scored 1.1232 against an incumbent mean of 1.1145, so it is worse by 0.0087 bpb (lower is better). A negative z is the right sign for a worse candidate under the convention z = (incumbent mean - candidate) / sd.

I could not recompute z independently because the incumbent standard deviation was not given. Working backwards, the reported z = -1.543 implies sd ≈ 0.0087 / 1.543 ≈ 0.0056. That is plausible but cannot be checked.
There is only one candidate run, so the evidence is weak. Still, the effect points the wrong way, so spending a replicate slot on it is hard to justify.
